summary: Documented path works on develop: --import, first-line import and NODE_OPTIONS give identical telemetry; --require still works but prints a 'no longer supported' banner the docs do not mention. Gaps: the verify step's 'My First Test Transaction' produces no transaction envelope under the default stream lifecycle (span envelope only); plain node:http segment spans are named 'GET' with no source; debug:true prints no SDK name, version or runtime; the ordering warning is overly strict for ESM first-line imports.

Documented path works on develop: --preload, bunfig preload, first-line import, --watch and a Bun.build bundle with the plugin all deliver the same errors, Bun.serve spans, fetch spans with headers and logs. The guide's claim that auto-instrumentation does not work with bundled code is refuted for runtime instrumentation. Gaps: two warnings about missing channel injection on the documented path that no page mentions; Bun error events carry no transaction field; no transaction envelope under the stream lifecycle; debug output names no SDK or runtime; installing the tarballs needs an overrides block (tarball artifact, not a guide defect).

The quick start path works on develop: first-line hook import, the --import flag form and deno serve all deliver errors with context lines and app:// paths, Deno.serve spans and logs. Confirmed gaps: no http.client span and no trace headers on outgoing fetch (K2); Deno.serve spans are named by method only, a URLPattern route gets no name; no transaction envelope under the stream lifecycle; no init banner with SDK or runtime on Deno. The shipped guide's flags (--allow-net, --allow-read) crash the app with NotCapable from the vendored debug package when the hook line is present, and without the hook they silently drop server_name, OS version, context lines and app:// paths. Nothing warns when the hook is absent. The bare --import=@sentry/deno/import form still fails.

withSentry with nodejs_compat works on develop at the documented compatibility_date floor: errors, one http.server span per request, http.client span with propagation headers, logs. The Vite plugin wraps the entry without withSentry in the source and without any experimental flag. Gaps: @sentry/cloudflare/nodejs_compat and Sentry.wrapRequestHandler from the main entry do not exist on develop although the guide shows both; the Vite plugin reads its options from an undocumented instrument.server.* file and falls back silently, and a bare sentryCloudflareVitePlugin() is a silent no-op when the wrangler config is not default-named; server spans are all named GET with source url and error events carry no transaction field; wrangler dev stack traces have no context lines; the segment span reports status ok on a 500; errors inside ctx.waitUntil() are never captured; the request entry with nodejs_als only works with the static lifecycle and sends transaction envelopes; debug output names no SDK or runtime.

variants.Vite plugin without withSentry: partial (works once wranglerConfigPath is set; options file undocumented)

summary: npm path delivers errors, pageload and navigation spans, http.client spans with headers on localhost, logs, sessions with the v11 page lifecycle and unhandled status, and a buffer replay once the session is older than five seconds. Defects: the tracing verify snippet is a SyntaxError (await in a non-async function); the CDN tab names bundle.tracing.min.js while adding replayIntegration(), which records nothing; Sentry.logger and Sentry.metrics are silent no-ops on the tracing CDN bundles; the documented tracePropagationTargets drops headers on 127.0.0.1; no contexts.browser/os/device on events; debug output names no SDK or browser; the commonjs, esm, esm-without-import, late-initialization and lightweight install pages are Node-only and never render for the browser.
